title: Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli unhurt after car crash in San Marino
content:
Kimi Antonelli was involved in a road car accident near his home in San Marino on Saturday, but the Mercedes Formula 1 driver walked away unharmed.

The incident occurred in Serravalle, San Marino on Saturday night. No other vehicles were involved.

In a statement supplied to The Athletic, a Mercedes team spokesperson said: “We can confirm that Kimi was involved in a traffic accident on Saturday night close to his home in San Marino.

“The police attended the scene, after being called by Kimi. His was the only car involved and while his vehicle was damaged, Kimi was completely unhurt.”

Italian newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport reported that law enforcement is investigating the cause and details of the incident, which it said involved Antonelli’s Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Motorsport Collectors Edition supercar.

Antonelli, 19, is scheduled to take part in the second test of the F1 preseason this week, which is taking place in Bahrain. He is expected to share 50 percent of the three-day running with his Mercedes teammate, George Russell.

Antonelli only obtained his road car driving license in January 2025, when he was 18 years old.

His motorsport career has featured rapid progression up the single-seater ranks, as he made his debut with Mercedes in the 2025 F1 season after only four years of car racing. Antonelli replaced seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton as Russell’s teammate.

The Italian finished seventh out of 20 drivers in the 2025 standings, three places and 169 points behind Russell. After a solid start, he endured a poor mid-season run of results before recovering impressively to end the season with three podium finishes (Montreal, São Paulo and Las Vegas).

Antonelli’s 2025 resurgence coincided with Mercedes’ decision to abandon a major rear suspension upgrade mid-season. His drive to second place in both the sprint race and GP in Brazil combined to produce his best overall weekend result of his rookie F1 campaign.

The 2026 season is expected to be critical for Mercedes, which enters as the preseason favorite thanks to the change in engine design rules.

The team’s High Performance Powertrains division has produced a design that generates more power than rivals thanks to a loophole discovered in the rules.

This development, which is worth up to 0.4-seconds per lap in extra speed, is currently being assessed by motorsport’s governing body, the FIA.

In a video released on Monday, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis said: “Our intention is to solve (the engine rules debate) for the start of the season.”

“We don’t want to have controversies. We want people to be competing on the track and not in the court room or in the stewards’ room. And that’s what we’re trying to do.”

Tombazis added: “We are determined to make this a championship of competition between the best drivers, the best engineers, the teams, but not a championship of rule interpretation. We want it to be a championship of engineering prowess, as well as driving prowess, but not of who is a smarter rule interpreter.”

But if Mercedes’ engine is ruled legal — something team boss Toto Wolff insisted was already the case in a fiery broadside towards rival engine builders last week — Antonelli has a significant chance of claiming a maiden F1 win and forcing a championship challenge alongside Russell this season.
